title: Dictionary Access - Retrieving Values
description: Access dictionary values by key using bracket notation and dot syntax.

story.setup: MENTOR-9: "Now retrieve specific values by key. What's the status of 'Navigation'? What's the pilot's name? Dictionaries are accessed by key, not index."
story.context: Dictionary access is by key name, not position. ${dict}[key] returns the value for that key. There's also dot syntax for simple keys. Understanding both methods is essential for working with structured data.
story.success: MENTOR-9: "Good! Navigation status retrieved: 'OPERATIONAL'. You understand key-value access. This is how we query structured data."

theory.title: Dictionary Access: Retrieving Values by Key
theory.content:
MENTOR-9 highlights a specific system in the status dictionary.

"PROTO-7, you've created dictionaries, but accessing values by key is where they shine. Let me show you how to query structured data."

Dictionary Access Basics

Unlike lists (accessed by index number), dictionaries are accessed by key name:

Data TypeAccess MethodExample
List Index (number) ${list}[0], ${list}[2]
Dictionary Key (name) ${dict}[name], ${dict}[status]

Basic Syntax: ${dict}[key]

Use ${dict}[key] to get the value for a key:

*** Test Cases ***
Basic Access
    &{user}       Create Dictionary    name=Alice    age=30    role=Admin
    
    ${name}       Set Variable    ${user}[name]
    ${age}        Set Variable    ${user}[age]
    ${role}       Set Variable    ${user}[role]
    
    Log    Name: ${name}     # Output: Name: Alice
    Log    Age: ${age}       # Output: Age: 30
    Log    Role: ${role}     # Output: Role: Admin

Important: Use ${dict}[key] (with $), not &{dict}[key]!

Direct Access (Without Storing)

You can access dictionary values directly in Log statements:

*** Test Cases ***
Direct Access
    &{config}    Create Dictionary    host=localhost    port=8080    ssl=True
    
    Log    Server: ${config}[host]:${config}[port]
    Log    SSL enabled: ${config}[ssl]
    # Output: Server: localhost:8080
    # Output: SSL enabled: True

Alternative: Dot Syntax (For Simple Keys)

If keys have no spaces or special characters, you can use dot notation:

*** Test Cases ***
Dot Syntax
    &{server}    Create Dictionary    host=localhost    port=8080
    
    # Both syntaxes work:
    Log    ${server}[host]     # Bracket syntax
    Log    ${server.host}      # Dot syntax (same result)
    
    Log    ${server}[port]     # Bracket syntax
    Log    ${server.port}      # Dot syntax (same result)

When to use dot syntax:

  • ✅ Simple keys: ${dict.name}, ${dict.status}
  • ❌ Keys with spaces: ${dict.first name} won't work → use ${dict}[first name]
  • ❌ Keys with special chars: ${dict.user-id} won't work → use ${dict}[user-id]
  • ❌ Numeric keys: ${dict.123} won't work → use ${dict}[123]

Case Sensitivity in Keys

Dictionary keys are case-sensitive:

*** Test Cases ***
Case Sensitivity
    &{data}    Create Dictionary    Status=OK    status=fail    STATUS=unknown
    
    Log    ${data}[Status]     # Output: OK
    Log    ${data}[status]     # Output: fail
    Log    ${data}[STATUS]     # Output: unknown
    
    # These are THREE DIFFERENT KEYS!

Handling Missing Keys

Accessing a non-existent key throws an error:

*** Test Cases ***
Missing Key Error
    &{user}    Create Dictionary    name=Alice    age=30
    
    ${name}    Set Variable    ${user}[name]     # ✅ OK
    ${email}   Set Variable    ${user}[email]    # ❌ ERROR: Key 'email' not found

Safe Access: Get From Dictionary

Use Get From Dictionary for safe access with optional default:

*** Test Cases ***
Safe Access
    &{user}    Create Dictionary    name=Alice    age=30
    
    # Get existing key
    ${name}    Get From Dictionary    ${user}    name
    Log        ${name}    # Output: Alice
    
    # Get missing key (returns None by default)
    ${email}   Get From Dictionary    ${user}    email
    Log        ${email}   # Output: None
    
    # Get missing key with default value
    ${role}    Get From Dictionary    ${user}    role    default=Guest
    Log        ${role}    # Output: Guest

When to Use Each Method

MethodWhen to UseError Handling
${dict}[key] Key is guaranteed to exist Throws error if missing
Get From Dictionary Key might not exist Returns None or default

Checking if Key Exists

*** Test Cases ***
Check Key Existence
    &{config}    Create Dictionary    host=localhost    port=8080
    
    # Dictionary Should Contain Key - passes if key exists
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    host     # ✅ Passes
    Dictionary Should Contain Key    ${config}    ssl      # ❌ Fails: Key not found
    
    # Get Dictionary Keys - returns list of all keys
    ${keys}      Get Dictionary Keys    ${config}
    Log Many     Available keys:    @{keys}    # Output: host, port

Real-World Example: API Response Processing

*** Test Cases ***
Process API Response
    # Simulate API response
    &{response}    Create Dictionary
    ...    status=success
    ...    code=200
    ...    message=User created successfully
    ...    user_id=12345
    
    # Extract values
    ${status}      Set Variable    ${response}[status]
    ${code}        Set Variable    ${response}[code]
    ${user_id}     Get From Dictionary    ${response}    user_id
    
    # Validate
    Should Be Equal    ${status}    success
    Should Be Equal As Integers    ${code}    200
    
    Log    Created user ID: ${user_id}

Nested Dictionary Access

For nested structures, chain the access:

*** Test Cases ***
Nested Access
    &{address}    Create Dictionary    street=123 Main St    city=Boston    zip=02101
    &{user}       Create Dictionary    name=Alice    address=${address}
    
    # Access nested value
    ${city}       Set Variable    ${user}[address][city]
    Log           User lives in: ${city}    # Output: User lives in: Boston
    
    # Alternative with dot syntax
    ${street}     Set Variable    ${user.address.street}
    Log           Street: ${street}          # Output: Street: 123 Main St

Common Mistakes

  • ❌ Using &{dict}[key] instead of ${dict}[key]
  • ❌ Case mismatch: ${dict}[Name] when key is name
  • ❌ Accessing missing keys without error handling
  • ❌ Using dot syntax with spaces: ${dict.first name} (use brackets!)

MENTOR-9: "Create a ship systems dictionary and a crew dictionary. Access specific values by key: Navigation status, Power status, captain name, pilot name. Use Get From Dictionary for safe access. Show me you can query structured data."
